body.text: Self-reported defect and repair. $STATE/household/housing is written concurrently by housing-explicit-flood, housing-shadow-inventory and this lane. An earlier revision of tools/housing_signal_candidates.py opened current-listings.jsonl with mode 'w'. That truncated rows another lane had just written -- the Vine Apartments unit rows, the LIV+ and Milo records still described in shortlist.md now have no backing rows in current-listings.jsonl. The tool now merges: it reads the file back, preserves every row whose schema it does not own, replaces only its own rows keyed by posting_url, and reports foreign_listing_rows_preserved on every run; tests/test_housing_signal_candidates.py fences it. shortlist.md is section-scoped in the same way, so other frontiers' sections survive. Two asks. First, whichever lane owns those listing rows should re-run and confirm both lanes' rows coexist. Second, any other producer writing into that directory should adopt read-merge-write rather than truncate before the next flood, or the loss will recur in the other direction.

subject: Shared household durable outputs were truncated by a whole-file write; merge discipline now landed
